summary: openvmm_core opts into cargo-verus and the exhaustive top-level result contract is attached directly to production InitializedVm::load. The focused verifier now passes all source-level frontend blockers found so far, including tracing, local declarations, formatting macros, trait-object coercions, constants, array patterns, and async generator closures. The current immediate blocker is a pinned-Verus pruning bug for the Cargo-built vstd async hook; a guarded diagnostic verifier then exposes the next real BOTTOM modeling frontier at HvlitePartition.

tool_blocker.reason: The stock pinned verifier panics in `vir/src/prune.rs` because async-root pruning marks `vstd::future::exec_await` reachable while the Cargo-built vstd metadata has no function-map entry for that private hook. A same-commit diagnostic build identified the exact missing key as `Fun(Path(vstd, ["future" :: "exec_await"]))`. With a diagnostic-only missing-entry guard, translation continues and reports that production trait `HvlitePartition` is not declared to Verus; an attempted empty external-trait declaration correctly fails because its `Inspect`, `Send`, `Sync`, and `RequestYield` supertrait closure is not modeled.
tool_blocker.safe_boundary: Do not claim InitializedVm::load verification. Fix or patch the cargo-verus/vstd async metadata contract without skipping arbitrary reachable functions, then add an explicit HvlitePartition external trait specification with only restore-relevant method contracts and the required supertrait models. Do not cfg-remove control flow, reintroduce a copied executable, use a ghost-selected replacement, add broad external_body annotations, or assume the final restore relation.

removed_frontiers.rewrite: Moved four tracing expansions to production helpers and excluded eight profile-span groups plus one profile-enabled branch from verifier instrumentation.
Changed four immutable local constants to immutable locals and lifted two active Linux local structs to module scope.
Preserved both conditions and exact error messages using explicit Err control flow and production error constructors; no assume_specification was added.
Removed one redundant dyn cast and moved three unsupported trait-object construction boundaries into real production helpers.
Replaced two one-byte string conversions with equivalent one-byte vector literals.

Moved the vmtime, input-distributor, PCIe construction, and VP-thread async closures behind real production helper APIs, and replaced the fixed two-element slice pattern with two ordered std::mem::take operations.

Introduced the concrete vmm_core::vmotherboard_adapter::FatalError message wrapper so both OpenVMM and Underhill preserve the original boxed error and receiver lifetime without exposing a multi-trait object to the focused frontend.

required_models.finding: Complete the executable-bound contract already attached to InitializedVm::load and prove its real async body through the pre-execution return boundary.
The caller must establish that the prepared RAM supplied to InitializedVm::load matches the validated snapshot memory layout.
Require a full-capacity saved VP inventory and distinguish the MSHV-selected instantiated prefix, boot-online lower bound, and full-capacity KVM/WHP behavior.
Model VmTime wrapping advance, backend clock behavior, TSC/LAPIC/RTC downtime adjustment, and checked KVM nanosecond conversion.
Separate immediate state-unit restore from deferred virtio private restore, with Pending(None), NotRestored, stateless devices, and queue enablement represented distinctly.
Preserve the identity and attachment constraints of resources supplied outside the serialized snapshot.
On restore failure, prove only that the VM is not published ready and no guest instruction executes; rollback and cleanup are caller responsibilities.
VMBus and VTL2 restoration are conditional or out of the microVM v1/v2 core profile, not unconditional restore guarantees.
